I’ve been managing a branch with over 50 staff for nearly a decade, and lately, I just can’t keep up—even though nothing’s changed at work, people keep giving me sideways looks, and I know they’re talking about me. I hear them mutter things like “she’s compromised” or “we know what she did,” even when no one’s speaking. Sometimes I smell burning paper—it’s sharp and sour—and no one else notices. It happens in meetings, in the car, anywhere. 

About three months ago, this all started getting worse. I find myself pacing my office after closing, unable to sit still, like something’s chasing me from the inside. My husband says I’ve been talking to the walls. 

I did go through a bad incident years ago—armed robbery at the branch, I was held at gunpoint—but that’s over. These voices and smells? They’re not about that. They're about being watched now, about hidden messages in the morning announcements on the radio meant just for me. That robbery was terrifying, but this? This feels like a completely different war.
D005-D018_h024.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D018_h025.question:
I’ve been having these strange thoughts and sensations for about three months now. I keep tasting something metallic, like blood, even when I’m not eating anything—just out of the blue. It’s unsettling. I also catch myself doing odd little gestures, like adjusting my glasses over and over or folding papers a certain way for no reason. My coworkers have noticed, I think.

Lately, I’ve become convinced my partner is being unfaithful. We haven’t even been close in years, but this idea won’t let go—it feels like proof is everywhere, even though there’s nothing real to back it up. I see the way people look at me, or *think* I see, and it all feels like a sign.

I should mention, a few years ago, I went through something traumatic—assaulted walking home late after a shift. It still haunts me sometimes. But these delusions and tastes? They don’t feel connected. They just show up out of nowhere, not during flashbacks or nightmares. I don’t jump at loud sounds or avoid places like I used to. This feels different—like my mind is creating its own reality.
D005-D018_h025.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
